Scratch scripts are in C:\Users\ahrar\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\E--Projects-SAS\aeac90fa-d510-40d8-a309-ad58f8606230\scratchpad\r3wf\a1\: a1_synth.py (belief algebra, planner scale invariance, swept rule), a1_front.py (per-step fate of mass near the fire), a1_rec.py, a1_nunf.py and a1_zero.py (recorded fb3 JSON, read-only).

HEADLINE FINDINGS
1. No decision reads the DEAD mass (verified). `belief.dead` is used only in measure's normalisation (victim_search_belief.py:208-211), in burn_over (:226) and in summary() (:245). Of the derived quantities, only `n_unfound` drives a decision (the R-1 switch, searcher_targeting.py:185). expected_unfound_alive and coverage_share appear only in summary(). The planner reads n_unfound, intensity() = n_unfound*p, p and last_cover, and nothing else.
2. The Bayes target choice is invariant to multiplying p (or lambda) by any positive constant, up to floating-point near-ties. This covers the s>0 filter, pre-rank, top-M, exact gain, score, tie-breaks, the order of free searchers and the coordination conditioning. Proof by linearity, plus 60 synthetic planner calls with 0 target mismatches at c = 0.5, 0.0022, 1e-3 and 0.37. So the DEAD share by itself changes no target. Burn-over acts only through (a) the SHAPE of p: it removes the fraction p_bo of the mass on burning cells only, with no renormalisation; and (b) the swept rule, and only locally.
3. The report's section-15 claim "(i) ... a global loss of alive mass to DEAD looks like a sweep" (outputs/fix3b_rescreen_report.txt:409-410) is WRONG, as the lead suspected.
   - Measure divides the uncovered alive mass and DEAD by the same z = 1 - r. A held target whose disc was not covered therefore has its Sp RAISED by 1/(1 - r).
   - Burn-over changes only burning cells and never renormalises.
   - Synthetic check: DEAD went 0.2 -> 0.333 while Sp at the held target went 0.4 -> 0.667, and there was no drop_swept.
   - Burn-over can trigger drop_swept only when the target's disc overlaps burning cells. Worst case (all of the disc's mass on burning cells, nothing else changing): 14 steps at p_bo 0.1, 3 steps at 0.5.
4. DEAD-share algebra (the total p.sum() + dead = 1 is invariant; the recorded summaries agree within 1e-6 in all 10 arms x 16 runs):
   - Measure sends D -> D/(1 - r). The share rises by the factor 1/(1 - r) without adding any DEAD mass. Equivalently, the dead:alive odds rise by 1/(1 - f), where f = r/A is the fraction of the alive mass swept that step.
   - Burn-over sends D -> D + p_bo * (alive mass on burning cells).
   - Closed form with no further burn-over: D_t = D_s / (D_s + A_s * prod(1 - f_k)). Any seed D_s > 0 is pushed past 0.5 by sweeping alone, so any p_bo > 0 can fail R-3.
   - At p_bo = 0, dead stays exactly 0: it starts at 0.0, measure keeps 0/z = 0, and burn_over returns early.
5. Setting SEARCHER_BELIEF_BURNOVER = 0:
   - Path: common_fixed_variables.py:214 -> agents.fix3b_param (agents.py:2209-2215; float(), NaN falls back to the default, no clamp) -> wildfire_model._fix3b_motion_params (:2734) -> MotionParams.burnover -> burn_over (victim_search_belief.py:217: `if not burning or p_bo <= 0.0: return`).
   - Nothing rejects or clamps 0. Negative values also act as 0. Values above 1 are not clamped.
   - One test pins the value: tests/test_searcher_targeting.py:462-468 test_burn_over_ships_at_the_ruled_value. Line 466 asserts the cfv text "SEARCHER_BELIEF_BURNOVER = 0.1". Line 468 asserts MotionParams().burnover == 0.1, which changes only if the dataclass default at victim_search_belief.py:105 is also changed. The fallback default at wildfire_model.py:2734 (0.1) and the comment at common_fixed_variables.py:211-213 should change with it.
   - Tests that pass 0.5 explicitly (:171-180, :199-206) are unaffected. The integration test (:401-422, sum == 1) still holds.
6. Under burn-over 0:
   - No mass can flow INTO burning cells (predict's avail excludes burning destinations). Mass is captured only when a cell holding it ignites.
   - Interior burning cells (no available neighbour) keep all their mass in both modes, and it is scaled up by every renormalisation.
   - Per-step outflow from a fire-front cell: 10% in diffusion (stays 0.900), about 63% in flee (stays 0.368).
   - Captured mass is released into burnt-out cells when the cell stops burning, and then attracts searchers to the burnt ground once it is admissible.
   - The support of p, and with it the set of s>0 candidates and the fallback condition, does not depend on p_bo < 1 for the same trajectory. R-1 depends only on n_unfound.
   - n_unfound keeps counting victims that died unseen: verified in 18 recorded re-screen runs, where R-1 continuation never triggered (lo_continuation_steps = 0). This is the same at any p_bo. Because of scale invariance, the over-count has no effect on decisions.
7. Other findings:
   - searcher_targeting.py:188 computes S = disc_convolve(lam) and never uses it (dead code).
   - A Bayes target can be up to Manhattan 2 closer to the fire than any cell the searcher can stand on (the route's goal radius), so its scored disc reaches about 2 rows deeper into the fire than the searcher's own disc will. Burn-over is currently the only thing that drains mass deeper in the fire, which no searcher disc can reach; at 0, that mass waits for burnout.

Burning cells are not recorded per step, so the split between the measure and burn-over channels in the 15 failures cannot be recovered from the recorded runs.

claims.claim: Where the belief update sits in MAPE-K. All of it runs in the post-move Knowledge stage of step t. adaptation_manager._run_post_move_cycle calls _detect_victims_in_uav_radius (adaptation_manager.py:171), then _refresh_knowledge_from_post_move_monitoring (:174-177). That calls wildfire_model._apply_monitoring_to_knowledge (wildfire_model.py:3449), which calls _update_victim_search_belief (:2480-2481). So every decision at step t+1 reads the belief as left by step t's post-move update. The prior and one launch measure at step 0 come from wildfire_model.py:2712-2724, built only when searcher_targeting_uses_belief(), i.e. modes 1-3 (wildfire_model.py:405-406; agents.py:2170-2172).

claims.claim: Order of operations inside one update (wildfire_model.py:2736-2773). (1) The burning and smoke sets are read once, after the move, at :2748 (the fire has already advanced in schedule.step). (2) PREDICT, modes 2 and 3 only (:2751-2752). (3) MEASURE on every UAV's post-move cell, all roles; the position comes from the monitoring buffer, or from a.pos if a UAV filed none (:2753-2764). (4) BURN-OVER, modes 2 and 3 only (:2765-2766), with the same burning set as predict. (5) detected_ids is extended from managed_victims[...].confirmed and from victim_runtime_model.victims (:2767-2771). This step's detections were already made at adaptation_manager.py:171, before the update. At mode 1 only measure (last_cover) acts. With SEARCHER_BELIEF_MOTION=0 the motion mode is 'off', which skips predict but still applies burn-over (:2728-2729, 2765).

claims.claim: Mass bookkeeping per operation; A = p.sum(), D = dead, and A + D = 1 is invariant. PREDICT (victim_search_belief.py:139-196) keeps A and D: the move weights plus w_stay sum to 1 per source cell, and moves go only to in-bounds neighbours that are not burning (:148-157, 188-196). So the DEAD share is unchanged and only the shape of p changes. MEASURE (:198-213): p <- p(1 - pd*cover); z = A - r + D = 1 - r; p <- p/z; D <- D/z. So A' = (A - r)/(1 - r), D' = D/(1 - r), and the total is 1. BURN_OVER (:215-226): on burning cells only, p(c) <- (1 - p_bo) p(c); D <- D + p_bo * sum over burning cells of p(c). The total is unchanged, there is no renormalisation, and p off the fire is unchanged. Recorded data: |alive_mass + dead_mass - 1| = 0 at 6-decimal rounding in every sampled summary of all 10 arms (fb3bdr, bfr, bdr2, bfr2, vs3r, bd, bf, bd2, bf2, vs3; 16 runs each).

Check 2: burn_over at p_bo 0, 0.1, 0.5 gives D + p_bo * M_B exactly, off-fire cells bit-identical. a1_rec.py: max |alive + dead - 1| = 0.00e+00 in every arm.

claims.claim: How the DEAD share evolves: D_{t+1} = D_t/(1 - r_t) + p_bo * B_t, where r_t is the alive mass inside this step's discs and B_t is the alive mass on burning cells after measure. Measure raises the DEAD share by the factor 1/(1 - r) and adds no DEAD mass. In odds form, D/A is multiplied by A/(A - r) = 1/(1 - f), where f = r/A is the fraction of the remaining alive mass swept that step. Closed form with no further burn-over after step s: D_t = D_s / (D_s + A_s * prod_k(1 - f_k)). The share passes 0.5 once the unswept alive mass A_s * prod(1 - f_k) falls below D_s. Example: a seed D_s = 0.05 passes 0.5 after 94.7% of the alive mass has been swept (0.95 * prod = 0.05 gives prod = 0.0526). So any p_bo > 0 can fail R-3 through sweeping alone. This is the exact Bayes posterior P(dead | no detection) under the belief's own model.

claims.claim: Which consumers react to a uniform rescaling of p (a change in the DEAD share alone) and which to a change in its SHAPE. (1) n_unfound: neither; it is a count. (2) lam in choose(): not to a rescale (see A1-3a); yes to a shape change, because S_c, the pre-rank, g and the score are all mass-weighted. (3) Sp / swept: not to a rescale that applies at both issue and now; not invariant to a change of scale BETWEEN issue and now, but no code path scales p down uniformly (see A1-4b); yes to local shape changes. (4) last_cover: neither; burn_over and predict never touch it, only measure writes it (victim_search_belief.py:212). (5) dead, expected_unfound_alive, coverage_share: no decision effect at all.

Proof that the Bayes choice is invariant to lambda -> c*lambda for any c > 0. disc_convolve and dilate-mask sums are linear (victim_search_belief.py:56-66), so S_c -> c S_c and g -> c g. The filter s <= 0 (:294) keeps the same cells because the sign is preserved. The pre-rank s/max(L, L0) scales by c, so the sort (-pre, L, cell) at :300 keeps its order. Battery, top-M and min-dist do not involve lam (:297, 302-306). The score g/max(L, L0) scales by c, so the key (score, -L, (-x, -y)) at :312 keeps its argmax. The 'alone' order at :328 uses -(score), with +1.0 for None; non-None scores are > 0 because g >= S_c[c] > 0, so the order is kept. Coordination: the claimed masks depend on geometry only (:263, 365), and lam*~claimed is linear (:326, 332, 366). Caveat: when c is not a power of two, floating-point rounding could in principle flip an exact near-tie.

claims.claim: What the swept rule compares. 'S at issue' is Sp at the chosen target, where Sp = disc_convolve(belief.p) over the radius-8 disc of p (ONE victim's posterior, not lambda) (:191, 317, 354). It is computed in the pre-move planning stage of the issuing step, from the belief after the previous step's post-move update. 'Sp now' is the same p-based quantity recomputed every step at :191 and tested at :253 for held targets, only while eff is 2 or 3. The issued-log field S (index 5 of fb3['issued']) is this p-based value; G (index 4) is the lam_cond-based gain.

Which belief operations can lower Sp at a held target T. MEASURE: Sp(T) -> (Sp(T) - covered part of the disc)/(1 - r). With no overlap it RISES by 1/(1 - r) >= 1. It falls only when the disc of T is itself swept enough that the removed share exceeds the inflation. BURN_OVER: Sp(T) -> Sp(T) - p_bo * (mass on burning cells inside the disc of T). This is purely local, and nothing changes when the disc has no burning cell. PREDICT: conserves mass but can move it out of the disc (flee away from the fire, diffusion spreading a peak). A detection elsewhere does not change p (test :191-196, and the LOW-3 test :375-384 pins no sweep). Therefore global DEAD-share growth CANNOT trigger drop_swept: it comes from (a) measure renormalisation, which raises an uncovered target's Sp, or (b) burn-over elsewhere, which leaves Sp(T) untouched. Burn-over triggers drop_swept only when the target's disc overlaps burning cells. The report claim (i) at fix3b_rescreen_report.txt:409-410 is wrong.

claims.claim: How predict treats mass near and on the fire. Mass never moves INTO a burning cell in either mode: avail[k] requires the destination neighbour to be in bounds and not burning (victim_search_belief.py:148-156). DIFFUSION (q = 0.1): any cell with at least one available neighbour moves exactly 0.1 of its mass per step, split equally (:160-162). That includes a burning FRONT cell, which keeps 0.900 per step. An interior burning cell (k = 0) keeps 1.000. FLEE: the alarm logistic on Euclidean distance d to fire is 0.966 at d = 0 and 0.5 at d = 5; the softmax gain is d(n) - d(c) (:164-187). A front burning cell keeps 0.368 per step (0.632 leaves), an interior one keeps 1.000. A non-burning cell adjacent to the fire keeps 0.351; one at 6 cells (y = 14 vs a fire edge at y = 20) keeps 0.751; one at 10 cells keeps 0.957. So burn-over hits a large standing front mass in mode 2 but mostly interior mass captured at ignition in mode 3. The latter is inferred to fit the report's observation that lowering p_bo reduced failures in the diffusion arms (14 -> 9) but not in the flee arms (4 -> 6).

claims.claim: Which near-fire mass a searcher disc can ever clear. Searchers move only over admissible cells: not burning, not strict smoke, not another UAV's cell, and at Manhattan distance >= clearance = min(d0, SEARCHER_ROUTE_CLEARANCE = SEARCHER_GATE_NEAR_RANGE = 6) from every burning cell (uav_executor.py:2390-2440; agents.py:2064, 2089). The detection disc is Euclidean radius 8 (197 cells). Against a straight front a searcher at Manhattan 6 covers burning cells only 0..2 deep ((x + 6)^2 <= 64 gives x <= 2), slightly deeper at corners (for example (2,2) of a quadrant fire from (-3,-3): 25 + 25 = 50 <= 64). Mass deeper inside a burning region cannot be cleared by any searcher while the region burns. Smoke cells are also not admissible, which pushes searchers further out. Measure uses every UAV's disc including fire trackers (wildfire_model.py:2753-2761); whether trackers fly near enough to clear the fire interior was not checked. Target goals may lie up to Manhattan 2 closer to the fire than any admissible cell (route goal radius, uav_executor.py:2443-2463; drop_reached when route[1] == 0, searcher_targeting.py:247). So the scored target disc can reach about 2 rows deeper than the disc the searcher actually flies.

claims.claim: Where alive mass on burning cells goes each step at p_bo = 0. Front cells leak 0.1 per step (mode 2) or about 0.63 per step (mode 3) to non-burning neighbours. Interior cells hold all of it. Mass cannot flow into the fire, so the fire's absolute mass grows only by (a) igniting cells that hold mass and (b) the shared renormalisation 1/(1 - r), which scales every uncovered cell. The fire's RELATIVE share of p therefore rises as the rest is searched, but the fire cannot concentrate mass by inflow. On burnout the mass sits on burnt cells and becomes coverable once admissible. dead stays 0, so p.sum() = 1 and lambda = n_unfound * p always.

claims.claim: R-1 continuation, fallback and swept at p_bo = 0. R-1: eff = 1 iff mode == 1 or n_unfound == 0 (:185), independent of p_bo. Fallback: support(p) does not depend on p_bo < 1 for the same trajectory, because predict's support depends only on burning/avail, measure zeroes exactly the covered cells, and burn_over with p_bo < 1 scales but never zeroes. So the s>0 candidate set and whether choose() returns None are unchanged. Only which target wins (shape) changes, and through it the later trajectory. Swept: the local burn-over trigger disappears; Sp can then fall only through predict outflow or measure sweeping.

claims.claim: n_unfound keeps counting victims that died unseen, and this does not depend on burn-over. n_unfound = n_brief - |detected_ids| (victim_search_belief.py:229-231). detected_ids grows only from confirmed managed victims or victim_runtime_model entries (wildfire_model.py:2767-2771). confirmed is set by detection (:1461), by dispatch (:4926) and by rescue_executor.py:568; _check_fire_casualties marks the victim dead without confirming it (wildfire_model.py:5609-5680). That dispatch requires a prior detection is inferred, not checked. Recorded: in all 80 re-screen runs the final n_unfound equals the number of never-detected victims. 18 runs end with one unseen, dead victim (fb3bdr 5, fb3bfr 6, fb3bdr2 2, fb3bfr2 2, fb3vs3r 3), and in each of them lo_continuation_steps = 0, so the R-1 rule never takes over. Because of scale invariance, the resulting over-count in lambda has no decision effect at any p_bo. At p_bo > 0 the belief ends near DEAD (final dead_mass 0.68-1.00 in those runs), but no code reads that, so the searchers keep looking either way.

claims.claim: A degenerate edge case. If every cell holding mass is covered in one measure, z = A - r + D: at p_bo 0 that is 0 and the `if z > 0` guard skips normalisation, so p stays all zero and p.sum() + dead = 0. The R-3 list reproduces exactly: 15 flagged victims and 268 non-flagged sampled victims. Only 10 of the 15 are distinct (seed, victim) pairs, because C_E, C_S and D_S on set 1 and B_N and B_S on set 2 are flagged in both the diffusion and the flee arm. 13 of the 15 are victim_0, which starts on the ring cell (40,25).

What the data show:
(1) The belief does NOT measurably steer targets away from the flagged victims compared with the others. Targets land within 8 cells of the victim at about chance rate in both groups (1.17x vs 1.25x chance over the full window; 2.09x vs 2.25x late).
(2) What sets the flagged victims apart is motion and position, not targeting:
- They move about 3x as often (0.119 vs 0.043 moves per window step).
- Their undetected window is about 6x longer (median 165 vs 27.5 steps).
- In the high-DEAD period they sit at the map edge: 78.7% of steps within 4 cells of the edge, median edge distance 1.
- They sit in neighbourhoods the fleet had NOT searched recently (8-cell disc covered in the last 30 steps: 0.17, against 0.47 for the grid).
- In 49.7% of high-DEAD steps the victim's own cell had been cleared earlier (median 125 steps before), so it moved into searched ground. The figure for non-flagged victims is 0.3%. This is a motion-model miss and is concentrated in C_S/D_S (4 runs at 84-100%). The other 11 sat in cells never covered.
(3) 9 of the 12 found were found by the targeting strategy itself (TARGETING label at t and t-1, active target 2-9 cells from the victim). The other 3 were found by fire trackers. That 25% fire-tracker share matches the non-flagged baseline (24.6%).
(4) Compared with the current searcher on the same seed, 11 of 15 were found later (median +128 steps, range +39 to never-vs-49). In all 11 the current searcher found the same victim at the same position, before the two victims' paths diverged. 3 were found earlier, and 1 was never found in either arm.
(5) G tracks n_unf*alive (Spearman 0.80; log-log Pearson 0.83 diffusion, 0.65 flee). When DEAD > 0.5, the median G falls about 500-fold (0.153 to 0.0003; flee arms 0.151 to 0.0000). In the flee arms half of the DEAD > 0.5 targets (171/348) were issued on G < 5e-6: the planner keeps choosing targets on essentially zero mass, which is what scale invariance implies. The belief's expected number of unfound alive victims at those issues has median 0.035-0.045.
(6) Association only: runs with a flagged victim have 3x the drop_swept per Bayes-delivered step (0.039 vs 0.012). Strategy steering does not collapse when DEAD is high: the share of searcher steps steered by targeting rises from 82-87% to 86-94%.
(7) The screen (burn-over 0.5) vs re-screen (0.1) shares above 0.5 per arm are in finding F7.

The R-3 check fails for a structural reason, and changing the burn-over value cannot fix it. I recommend option H: keep 0.1, record the R-3 FAIL as is, and replace the per-victim threshold with pre-registered calibration and belief-at-truth checks. Burn-over = 0 (A) is defensible, but it passes the check by construction. I am leaving the decision to you. 1. The claim in report section 15 is WRONG (verified; fix3b_rescreen_report.txt:409-411).
- The claim: "a global loss of alive mass to DEAD looks like a sweep".
- Before measure, p.sum() + dead = 1. predict conserves mass (victim_search_belief.py:188-196) and so does burn_over (:219-226).
- measure zeroes the covered cells, then divides p AND dead by z = 1 - (covered alive mass) <= 1 (:207-211).
- So for a held target whose disc is uncovered and not burning, Sp is left alone by burn-over elsewhere and multiplied by 1/z >= 1 by measure. Global DEAD growth only slows Sp's rise; it can never trigger drop_swept (searcher_targeting.py:253).
- Sp falls only through LOCAL loss inside the target's disc: coverage there, motion out of it, or burn-over on burning cells in it. The last one is the intended "the fire took its mass" channel (fix3b_part1.txt:261).
- Replacement wording: "(i) burn-over on burning cells inside a held target's disc looks like a sweep (by design); a global rise of DEAD only slows the rise of the target's mass and cannot cause a drop."

2. DEAD does not change which target is chosen (verified).
- Ranking ignores the overall scale of lambda: the checks are s > 0 (:293-295), the pre-rank s/max(L,L0) (:299) and g/max(L,L0) with key (score,-L,cell) (:310-312).
- The DEAD scalar is read only by the reported summaries: expected_unfound_alive (victim_search_belief.py:237-238) and the 10.5 POS(t) metric.
- Burn-over affects targeting only through the SHAPE of p near the fire and the local swept channel.

3. The DEAD share is a ratchet (verified).
- Every stage is linear and normalisation is one common scale, so dead_mass = d_raw/(d_raw + a_raw). d_raw (the raw mass burn-over moved) never shrinks; a_raw (the raw alive mass) never grows. So the DEAD share never decreases.
- Recorded data agree: 0 decreases in 5 600 sample pairs over all 10 Bayes arms (monotone.py).
- Because p is shared, the per-victim R-3 check is a RUN-LEVEL CLOCK: every alive victim detected after the run's first D > 0.5 sample fails.
- p_bo barely moves that clock. Median DEAD at step 100: BD-R 0.611 vs BD at 0.5 0.640; BF-R 0.104 vs 0.137 (dead_traj.py; not like-for-like because of R-1). Mass trapped in fire is 89-96% removed over a 21-30-step burn at any p_bo >= 0.1.
- The fire burns a median of 929-1348 of 2500 cells per arm, and coverage reaches 0.94-0.98 by step 200. So any p_bo > 0 fails R-3 for victims that stay undetected late.

4. Calibration (POST HOC, descriptive; triples are correlated, 10-15 distinct victims per high bin).

- Late in runs most undetected victims really are dead: at step 200, BF-R pooled has 11 dead vs 2 alive (calib.py).
- So the misspecification the data show is BD's fire-agnostic motion, which is the designed contrast, not the DEAD state as such.

5. Burn-over = 0 (option A), mechanically.
- dead stays exactly 0: burn_over returns at :217, and measure keeps dead at 0 (:211). The check passes by construction and detects nothing.
- Alive mass then persists on burning and burnt cells, where in the simulator any victim would already be dead (wildfire_model.py:5610-5641). How much: roughly the current DEAD share, median 0.92 BD-R / 0.46 BF-R at step 200 (inferred; it cannot be replayed because burning cells are not recorded).

6. Two facts about the code and docs.

Option H. Keep burn-over 0.1 and leave the belief and targeting unchanged (no src change). Record the R-3 FAIL verbatim.

What to pre-register for the measurement round (Part 1 section 18, fixed before any run):
- (1) calibration of the DEAD share against the true fate of undetected victims;
- (2) belief-at-truth (r_v) and its percentile;
- (3) the old R-3 count, exact per step, reported but not gating.

- Put the instrument in outputs/_fb3_probe.py. Truth must stay out of the managing system.
- Re-run the 80 Bayes strategy runs with the extended probe, about 80 min, and REQUIRE value identity with the recorded re-screen.

- (b) Target choice does not read it at all: ranking ignores the overall scale.
- (c) Every belief change that "passes" R-3 does so either by construction (A, E, I), so the check detects nothing, or unpredictably while staying a ratchet (C, D, F, K), and each adds a post-screen change.

- Primary 0, with sensitivity {0.1, 0.5}.
- The full 100-job re-screen (about 1 h 40), then the suite.
- The same instrument, made mandatory.
- POS(t) redefined from the mass the negative update removes.
- The third post-screen value disclosed.

analysis.replacement_instrument:
Placement: in outputs/_fb3_probe.py's step wrapper (:120-142), after the post-move belief update, EVERY step. It is record-only: no RNG draw and no simulation write.
- It reads true victim positions, so it lives in the evaluation probe, never in src_extension (the information boundary of 15.1(d)).
- Belief internals are read through class-level wrappers on VictimSearchBelief.measure and burn_over. Each wrapper reads p before and after and calls the original unchanged.

Per step, record:
(1) The 17.2 fields: dead_mass, alive_mass, n_unfound, the mass burn-over moved, and the alive mass the negative update removed before renormalising.
(2) For every victim alive (marker status not dead or rescued) and undetected (step < first [Victim Detection]) at the step:
- a_v = (sum of p over disc8(x_v)) / p.sum(). This is the alive-conditional mass in the Euclidean-8 disc around the victim's TRUE cell x_v. It does not depend on DEAD, so it is comparable across p_bo values (0, 0.1, 0.5) and across BD / BF.
- u_v = |disc8(x_v) ∩ H0 support| / |H0 support|.
- r_v = a_v / u_v (1 = as good as the uniform prior; < 1 = the belief disfavours the victim's area).
- pct_v = the share of non-band stride-2 candidate cells whose Sp exceeds Sp at x_v. This is where targeting would rank the victim's location.
(3) The burning and smoke sets (rows_uav already has the UAV cells). This enables an EXACT offline belief replay at any p_bo on the recorded trajectories. Validate it by reproducing the per-step summary to float precision before using it.
(4) At each drop_swept, the held target's Sp loss split into coverage / motion / burn-over.
(5) References: the LO arm builds p with measure only, no predict or burn-over (wildfire_model.py:2751-2752, :2765-2766). That gives a motion-free reference r_v. Optionally, a shadow belief for the CUR arm computed in the probe.

PRE-REGISTRATION (Part 1 section 18, before any measurement run; unit = run; bootstrap over runs; per arm and at every p_bo sensitivity point):
- PRIMARY belief-validity quantities: the median over alive-undetected victim-steps of log r_v, and the share of those steps with r_v < 1. Compared BF vs BD vs the LO reference, descriptive with CIs.
- DEAD calibration (when DEAD exists): reliability in the fixed bins [0, .25, .5, .75, .9, 1]; Brier vs climatology; observed alive above 0.5 vs the calibrated expectation sum(1 - D). A pre-stated two-sided criterion: over- or under-confidence when the observed count falls outside the 95% run-bootstrap interval of the expectation.
- The old R-3 count, exact per step, REPORTED, not gating.

Under option A, items (1)-(2) except the DEAD fields remain fully meaningful; the R-3 count is identically 0 and must be labelled vacuous.

Validation of the instrument itself: in the re-check, the 80 re-run Bayes runs must be value-identical to the recorded re-screen.
